Compaction is equivalent only if padding never advances the reference GRU state: zero embeddings alone are insufficient because recurrent biases can update hidden states. For LEFT-padded histories, gather valid tokens chronologically into right-padded prefixes before packing. Tokenwise linear projections, activations and LayerNorm over features preserve valid-token computations; LayerNorm spanning time does not. Training BatchNorm changes when padding or normalization groups are removed; evaluation BatchNorm preserves tokenwise behavior with identical fixed running statistics. These are deductions from PyTorch’s [GRU equations](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/generated/torch.nn.GRU.html), [LayerNorm](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/2.15/generated/torch.nn.LayerNorm.html) and [BatchNorm](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/2.15/generated/torch.nn.BatchNorm1d.html) definitions.

Elementwise embedding/output dropout preserves its distribution under compaction, but identical seeds do not guarantee identical token masks after reshaping/reordering; gather explicitly shared masks for parity tests. Preserve any sequence-shared dropout mask across timesteps. PyTorch GRU dropout acts between recurrent layers, excluding the last; it is inactive for a single layer. Packed/dense kernels need not reproduce identical stochastic draws. See [Dropout](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/2.15/generated/torch.nn.Dropout.html) and [GRU](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/generated/torch.nn.GRU.html).

Verification protocol: exclude zero-length rows from packing and explicitly preserve their defined fallback; never process a dummy token as history. Unpack, restore original batch order, and differentiably scatter outputs to original valid positions; remask after biased transformations. Read the final nonpadding position, never count−1 in LEFT-padded coordinates. Gather positives/negatives with identical indices, preserve causal next-item shifts and loss normalization. Compare valid features, scores, losses and every parameter gradient against an unpadded or state-masked reference using identical weights, dropout disabled/shared masks and numerical tolerances. Include empty, singleton, mixed-length, reordered and all-empty batches; perturb future tokens to test causality. These checks compare implementations of one model without fitting another predictor. [Packing/unpacking behavior](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.utils.rnn.pad_packed_sequence.html).
